#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 72 -c 1 -t 12h --job-name=soy_test_alignment --setattr=system.memory=216000M script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from -N 1)
# -n 72        : 72 tasks (from -n 72)
# -c 1         : 1 CPU per task (from --cpus-per-task=1)
# -t 12h       : 12 hour walltime (from -t 12:00:00)
# --job-name=soy_test_alignment : job name (from --job-name=soy_test_alignment)
# --setattr=system.memory=216000M : Total memory (72 tasks × 3000 MB/task = 216000 MB)
#
# Memory calculation:
# Slurm: --mem-per-cpu=3000 with --cpus-per-task=1 and -n 72
# Total: 72 tasks × 1 CPU/task × 3000 MB/CPU = 216000 MB = ~211 GB
# Flux: --setattr=system.memory=216000M for total node memory
# Note: Memory attribute syntax may vary by Flux version
# Alternative: --setattr=memory=216000M (verify for your Flux version)

# Original job name: soy_test_alignment
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=soy_test_alignment ...

# Output/Error redirection: /dev/null
# Original: --output=/dev/null --error=/dev/null
# Flux: Can be set at submission with --output=/dev/null --error=/dev/null
# Or omit from submission command to use default Flux output handling
# For this conversion, assuming user wants to discard output:
# Add to submission: --output=/dev/null --error=/dev/null

# Exclusive node access:
# Original: --exclusive flag for exclusive node allocation
# Note: Flux handles exclusivity through resource allocation
# By requesting all 72 tasks on 1 node (-N 1 -n 72), you effectively get exclusive
# access if the node has 72 cores total
# Performance impact: Without explicit exclusive flag, other jobs might share the node
# if not all resources are requested. Ensure -n matches the node's total core count
# or use Flux scheduling policies for exclusive allocation

# Email notification: jhgille2@ncsu.edu (BEGIN, END, FAIL events)
# Note: Flux does not have built-in email notification directives
# Performance impact: User must manually monitor job status or implement external
# monitoring solutions using flux job events, flux watch commands, or wrapper scripts
# Consider creating notification wrappers or using flux job attach with monitoring
# Email events: BEGIN, END, FAIL would need custom implementation

# Submit the pipeline as a job
# Original comment: Submit the pipeline as a job with srun job.sh
# Flux equivalent: flux batch [options] script.sh

# Load required modules
module load singularity

# Execute R script within Singularity container
# Direct execution without parallel launcher since this is a batch job
# The R script itself may handle parallelization with clustermq or similar
singularity exec conda.sif R CMD BATCH run.R

# Removing .RData is recommended.
# rm -f .RData

# Note on execution model:
# The original Slurm script allocates 72 tasks but runs a single R CMD BATCH
# This suggests the R script (run.R) uses clustermq or similar for parallel workers
# The 72 tasks allocation provides resources for worker processes spawned by R
# In Flux, the same model applies: allocate resources, let R manage parallelization
# If using clustermq with Flux, configure clustermq to use flux as the scheduler

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=216000M' may not be correct for all Flux versions. The attribute path 'system.memory' should be verified. Common alternatives include '--setattr=memory=216000M' or resource specification may need different syntax depending on Flux version.

The memory calculation (72 tasks × 3000 MB = 216000 MB) is mathematically correct, but the documentation should clarify this is total node memory, not per-task memory. Flux memory specifications typically apply to the entire allocation.
The submission command documentation is missing output/error redirection flags. The recommended command should include '--output=/dev/null --error=/dev/null' to match the original Slurm behavior.
Complete recommended submission command should be: 'flux batch -N 1 -n 72 -c 1 -t 12h --job-name=soy_test_alignment --setattr=system.memory=216000M --output=/dev/null --error=/dev/null script.sh'

The script allocates 72 tasks (-n 72) but the R CMD BATCH command is executed directly without using 'flux run' or similar launcher. While this works if R/clustermq manages parallelization internally, it's not utilizing Flux's task management. This is acceptable but should be noted.

Exclusive node access strategy relies on requesting 72 tasks assuming the node has exactly 72 cores. If nodes have more cores, this won't guarantee exclusivity. Consider documenting the node architecture or using Flux-specific exclusivity mechanisms if available.
The memory allocation of 216 GB (~211 GB) is very high. Verify that nodes in the target system have sufficient memory. If nodes have less than 216 GB, the job will fail to allocate.
No validation that the requested resources (72 cores, 216 GB memory) are actually available on target nodes. This could lead to jobs that never schedule.
The comment about clustermq configuration with Flux is helpful but incomplete. Should reference specific clustermq documentation or configuration examples for Flux backend.

#!/bin/bash

# Submit the pipeline as a job with srun job.sh

# Modified from https://github.com/mschubert/clustermq/blob/master/inst/LSF.tmpl
# under the Apache 2.0 license:
#SBATCH --job-name=soy_test_alignment
#SBATCH --output=/dev/null
#SBATCH --error=/dev/null
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=3000
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH -n 72
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH -t 12:00:00
#SBATCH --mail-user=jhgille2@ncsu.edu
#SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL

module load singularity
singularity exec conda.sif R CMD BATCH run.R

# Removing .RData is recommended.
# rm -f .RData
